title: SpaceInvite/set create has no manage_members permission enforcement
description:
Site: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/invite.rs:115-247 (handle_invite_set create branch). MemoryBackend create_object<SpaceInvite> in src/memory.rs:681-714 (the generic create_object) also performs zero permission check.

draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 §SpaceInvite/set (line 1290-1294): 'create accepts: spaceId (String, required), defaultChannelId (String, optional), expiresAt (UTCDate, optional), maxUses (UnsignedInt, optional). **Requires `"manage_members"` permission.**'

The same applies to destroy (line 1296): 'destroy revokes an invite. Requires manage_members permission or ownership of the invite.'

Per workspace AGENTS.md backend-canonical permission policy, permission enforcement lives in the backend. But the reference MemoryBackend's create_object<SpaceInvite> is the generic path — no SpaceInvite-specific gate, no caller_effective_permissions lookup, no consultation of required_permissions_for_op. ANY caller with JMAP access to the account can mint an invite for ANY Space whose id they can guess.

The handler also does no defense-in-depth pre-check.

Concrete trigger: in a deployment where account A has guest access to Space S, A calls SpaceInvite/set create with spaceId=S. Spec REQUIRES this to fail with forbidden (A lacks manage_members in S). Today it succeeds and yields a valid invite code that anyone can redeem.

Fix sketch:
1. Add ChatBackend::create_space_invite(&self, caller, account_id, space_id, ...) -> Result<SpaceInvite, BackendSetError> with the manage_members gate atomic with the create.
2. OR: keep the generic create_object surface and add a separate gate method may_create_space_invite(&self, caller, account_id, space_id) that handle_invite_set calls.
3. OR: extend apply_space_patch with an AddInvite variant gated via the existing pre-validation pass.

Whichever approach is chosen, both handler-side pre-check (defense in depth) and backend atomic enforcement must land — the workspace policy explicitly requires the backend re-verify, but the handler should fail-fast on obviously-unauthorized requests when identity is resolvable.
close_reason: Fixed in ca67f9fc: ChatBackend::may_set_space_invite hook called by handle_invite_set before create/destroy; MemoryBackend requires manage_members, destroy also allowed when createdBy == accountId. Tests: tests/space_invite_permissions.rs (3).
